title: Conductor ampacity table (up to 3 conductors, 30 C)
summary: The main ampacity table for insulated conductors rated up to 2000 V when no more than three current-carrying conductors share a raceway, cable, or direct burial and the ambient is 30 C. Columns are by insulation temperature rating; the 60 C, 75 C, and 90 C values for copper and aluminum are what the sizing calculator starts from.
fieldNotes: Pick the column by the weakest link: the conductor insulation rating or the equipment termination rating, whichever is lower (110.14(C)).
Apply ambient correction and bundling adjustment to the insulation column, then compare against the termination column.

title: Ampacity corrections and adjustments
summary: Reduces table ampacity when the ambient temperature is above 30 C, when more than three current-carrying conductors are bundled, or when conductors are in sunlight on a roof. Also lists what does not count as a current-carrying conductor, such as most neutrals on balanced circuits and equipment grounding conductors.
fieldNotes: Four to six current-carrying conductors: 80%. Seven to nine: 70%. Ten to twenty: 50%.
A raceway nipple 24 inches or shorter is exempt from the bundling adjustment.

title: Termination temperature limits
summary: Equipment terminations limit how much of a conductor's ampacity you can use. Unless the equipment is marked for a higher rating, circuits rated 100 A or less use the 60 C column and circuits over 100 A use the 75 C column, even when the conductor insulation is rated 90 C.
fieldNotes: Most modern breakers and lugs are marked 60/75 C, which lets you use the 75 C column for small circuits too.

title: Small conductor overcurrent limits
summary: Caps the overcurrent device for small conductors regardless of table ampacity: 15 A for 14 AWG copper, 20 A for 12 AWG copper, 30 A for 10 AWG copper, 15 A for 12 AWG aluminum, and 25 A for 10 AWG aluminum, unless a specific rule such as motor or tap provisions allows otherwise.

title: Branch-circuit conductor sizing and voltage drop guidance
summary: Branch-circuit conductors must have an ampacity of at least the noncontinuous load plus 125% of the continuous load before correction, and at least the full load after correction and adjustment. An informational note suggests keeping voltage drop to 3% on the branch circuit and 5% total with the feeder for reasonable efficiency; that guidance is advisory, not enforceable.

title: Maximum conduit fill percentages
summary: Limits how much of a raceway's cross-section conductors may occupy: 53% for one conductor, 31% for two, and 40% for three or more. A note allows 60% for a nipple not longer than 24 inches. Table 4 gives raceway areas and Table 5 gives conductor areas used with these percentages.

title: Feeder conductor sizing and voltage drop guidance
summary: Feeder conductors follow the same two-part sizing rule as branch circuits: at least the noncontinuous load plus 125% of the continuous load before correction, and at least the full load after correction and adjustment. The informational note repeats the 3% feeder and 5% combined voltage drop guidance, which is advisory.

title: Raceway internal areas by type and trade size
summary: Lists the internal cross-sectional area of each raceway type at each trade size, along with the 53%, 31%, 40% and 60% portions already worked out. The conduit fill calculator uses the 100% area and applies the Table 1 percentage.

title: Insulated conductor dimensions and areas
summary: Gives the approximate diameter and cross-sectional area of each insulated conductor type and size. THHN, THWN and THWN-2 share one set of values; XHHW and XHHW-2 share another. Add the areas of all conductors in the raceway and compare against the allowed portion from Table 4.
